questions.q: Why did the nose of Yahweh burn against Israel?
questions.a: The Israelite men began having sex with Moabite women, and the people ate and prostrated themselves to the Moabite gods.

questions.q: What god did Israel join in worshiping at Peor?
questions.a: Israel joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses to do to the leaders of the people?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to execute the leaders of the people and display their bodies publicly before Yahweh, so that Yahweh would stop being very angry with the Israelites.

questions.q: What did Moses tell the judges of Israel to do?
questions.a: Moses told each judge to execute his own men who had associated themselves with Baal of Peor.

questions.q: Where was the community of the people of Israel when a man brought a Midianite woman near to his brothers?
questions.a: When a man from the sons of Israel brought the Midianite woman near to his brothers, the people were weeping at the opening of the tent of meeting.

questions.q: What did Phinehas, son of Eleazar, do when he saw what happened with the Midianite woman?
questions.a: When Phinehas watched saw happened with the Midianite woman, he rose from the midst of the congregation and took a spear in his hand.

questions.q: What happened when Phinehas pierced the man of Israel and the woman?
questions.a: The plague was restrained from the sons of Israel.

questions.q: How many were the ones who died in the plague?
questions.a: The ones who died in the plague were 24,000.

questions.q: Why was Yahweh no longer angry with the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh was no longer angry because Phinehas wanted the Israelites to worship only Yahweh, just as much as Yahweh wants that.

questions.q: What did Yahweh call the covenant he gave to Phinehas?
questions.a: Yahweh called it his covenant of peace.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh make a covenant of everlasting priesthood with Phinehas?
questions.a: Yahweh made a covenant with Phinehas because he was zealous for Yahweh and had atoned for the people of Israel.

questions.q: What was the name of the Israelite man who was struck with the Midianite woman?
questions.a: His name was Zimri the son of Salu, a leader of a house of a father for the Simeonite.

questions.q: What was the name of the Midianite woman who was killed?
questions.a: Her name was Kozbi, daughter of Zur, a leader of a Midianite family.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Moses to treat the Midianites as enemies and attack them?
questions.a: God told Moses to treat the Midianites as enemies and attack them because they had treated Israel like enemies with their deceitfulness.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say Kozbi, the daughter of the leader of Midian, was to the Midianites?
questions.a: Yahweh said that Kozbi was their sister, that is, one of their own people.

commentary.text: The Israelites enticed by the daughters of Moab and Midian.
Phinehas puts Zimri and Cozbi to death.

Verses 1–5 The friendship of the wicked is more dangerous than their enmity; for none can prevail against God's people if they are not overcome by their inbred lusts; nor can any enchantment hurt them, but the enticements of worldly interests and pleasures. Here is the sin of Israel, to which they are enticed by the daughters of Moab and Midian. Those are our worst enemies who draw us to sin, for that is the greatest mischief any man can do us. Israel's sin did that which all Balaam's enchantments could not do; it set God against them. Diseases are the fruits of God's anger, and the just punishments of prevailing sins; one infection follows the other. Ringleaders in sin ought to be made examples of justice.
Phinehas, in the courage of zeal and faith, executed vengeance on Zimri and Cozbi. This act can never be an example for private revenge, or religious persecution, or for irregular public vengeance.

We read not that any Midianites died of the plague; God punished them with the sword of an enemy, not with the rod of a father. We must set ourselves against whatever is an occasion of sin to us, Mt 5:29, 30. Whatever draws us to sin, should be a vexation to us, as a thorn in the flesh. And none will be more surely and severely punished than those who, after Satan's example, and with his subtlety, tempt others to sin.
